body.x: Clonix (CEO Seung-Rhee Nam, www.xclonix.com) released its "NetClon" series, its disk duplicating and wiping device via network and disk network, at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The NetClon NC1000-16HL is a data duplicator and wiper system which can simultaneously connect to a 16-port network. NC1000 can duplicate through 16 ports at the same time whether th file is same or different at speeds up to 10GB/m. It has the ability to back-up, duplicate and delete various storage drives without having to detach the drive from the system.

The NetClon DC3000-16HL is a hard disk duplicator and wiper which can simultaneously duplicate and erase data from 16 ports. The device has both disk-to-disk and image-to-disk capabilities at speeds up to 12GB/m.

Top speed for wiping data is 20GB/m and it supports all five international methodologies of disk erasing. Data is erased by writing over the characters allowing the disk to be reused but the data becomes unrecoverable. It supports both Windows and Linux systems and can read/write to SAS/SATA/IDE HDD, SSD, CF, and SD. Its quick maintenance and customizing capabilities are its distinguishing features.

Also being previewed is the "WinClon," a unique backup and recovery solution for OS and application installed systems which stores important data in an image format. This solution has shown promise and is currently equipped in all Samsung PC and laptops.

A spokesperson for Clonix said, “We are looking to establish a foothold to venture into the American market through the upcoming CES 2015 exhibition. We believe our self-developed hardware, supported by our technology, will prove alluring to the overseas market.”

Clonix began in 2004 and has since continually showcased technology development and products in the system backup and security industry. From its original technology of system recovery software and products, it has continually expanded its business into other industries such as hard disk, SSD, eMMC memory duplication, and more.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
